description: The LongClaw desktop webview may use typed IPC/events and open one native folder picker. It has no frontend filesystem, shell, network, or process capability: where a command reaches the disk or the OS — reading a ticket, or handing one to the editor via open_ticket_file — the webview names a ticket key and Rust resolves the path inside the open project. install_command_line is the one command that writes outside a project folder, and it is the same shape rather than an exception to it: the webview asks for the longclaw command to be installed and names no path, and Rust decides that the link is /usr/local/bin/longclaw, that its target is this bundle's own binary, and that a file it did not create is never replaced. It is app-defined, so it runs under core:default and the permission list below is unchanged. The same shape covers the two GitHub commands (LC-257s, ADR 0015): open_repository asks for the LongClaw repository to be opened in the browser and star_count asks for its public star count, and both times Rust holds the address as a constant and the webview names nothing. open_attachment and reveal_attachment (LC-206) name a ticket key and an attachment record's file, and Rust holds the file to that ticket's registry and its attachments folder before macOS sees a path; open_attachment also refuses a file name macOS would run rather than show. reattach_attachment names the same two things plus the hash the panel read, and registers a file already in that folder. attach_bytes takes a pasted or dropped file's bytes as the request body with the project, ticket, hash and name as headers. choose_files_to_attach raises the system file picker from Rust and answers with an opaque token, a name and a size per file — never a path — and attach_chosen attaches by that token, so the webview can attach only a file the human picked. Both copy into that ticket's attachments folder only after Rust has checked the size and sniffed the content.
